name: AccentBar
title: AccentBar
summary: A thin 3px progress line filled with the signature gradient, available as the React `AccentBar` and as `.cr-accentbar` classes.
whenToUse: Use for quiet, passive progress: how far through a chapter, an audio teaching, a reading plan or an onboarding carousel.
Use on dark surfaces by default (app player, `.sec-ink` bands); use `.cr-accentbar-light` on white or `--off-white`.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for uploads, form steps or anything the user waits on; use Progress for that.
Do not use as a decorative rule; use Divider (`.thread`).

anatomy.description: A track (18% white on dark, 12% black on light) with a gradient fill from the left. No labels, no handle.
anatomy.markup: The HTML bar fills its parent's width; set a width on the parent, not on the bar.

props.name: width
props.description: Track width in px, or any CSS width such as "100%".

props.name: light
props.description: Light track (`rgba(0,0,0,.12)`) for white or off-white surfaces. The default track is for dark surfaces.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name ("John 3 read"). When given, the track gets `role="progressbar"` with value attributes.
Without it the bar is plain divs: show the value in text beside it.

react.notes: `import { AccentBar } from '@ism/ui'`. It renders the `.cr-accentbar` classes, so it matches the HTML below.

props.name: width
props.description: Track width in dp, or a percentage such as "100%".

props.name: light
props.description: Light track (`rgba(0,0,0,.12)`) for white or off-white surfaces. The default track (`rgba(255,255,255,.18)`) is for dark surfaces.

props.name: label
props.description:
Names what is progressing ("John 3 read"). When given the bar is exposed as a progressbar with its value;
without it the bar is hidden from screen readers, so show the value in text beside it.

props.name: GradientComponent
props.description:
Gradient view such as `LinearGradient` from expo-linear-gradient or react-native-linear-gradient. The fill is `gradient-signature`.
Without it the fill is a solid `gradient-violet` colour (never Horizon Blue).

variantNotes: States: empty (0%), partial, complete (100%). The fill is always `--gradient-signature`; it never changes colour for "done".

states.documented: empty (0%), partial, complete (100%). The fill is always `--gradient-signature`; it never changes colour for "done".
states.universal: See rules/states.md for the seven required states and their hooks.

rules: Fill with `--gradient-signature` only. Never solid Horizon Blue (`--horizon-blue`); blue is reserved for the one primary button.
Keep it 3px tall with a 2px radius. Do not thicken it into a progress bar.
One AccentBar per item. In a list of teachings, each row gets its own (see ListRow).
Pair it with a nearby text value when the number matters ("9:12 left", "Day 4 of 21").
Do not animate it on load; update it as real progress changes.

accessibility: In HTML, give the track `role="progressbar"`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and an `aria-label` naming what is progressing.
The React `AccentBar` gets the progressbar role and values only when you pass `label`. Without it the bar is plain `div`s: show the value in text beside it.
A 3px line alone is hard to see; never make it the only place progress is reported.
content: Labels name the thing, not the percentage: "John 3 read", "Reading plan: Gospel of John", "Audio teaching progress".
Visible companions are short: "60% read", "Day 4 of 21", "9:12 left".

<AccentBar progress={0.25} width="100%" light label="Reading plan" />
